recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current source satisfies FHIR-2964 after considering the original application and later boundary clarifications; adding more prose would duplicate current guidance and risk drift.
issue_request: FHIR-2964 was a Published FHIR-core Patient Care change request for the Initial Draft/DSTU1 Observation artifact. It asked that the introductions for Observation and Condition clearly differentiate when each resource should be used. The final Persuasive with Modification resolution directed Eric Haas to enhance the Observation introduction and Stephen Chu to enhance the Condition introduction.
initial_application: No explicit FHIR-2964-tagged commit was found. The historical source application appears in December 2014 SVN-era commits: a84a0c5884fdbcb5dcb003820bb86641e52d448e updated the Condition introduction with problem/diagnosis/concern scope and Observation boundary guidance, and 3ecf22e65d42355b0c19a59ecb149bfa6bc5ea5a updated Observation by removing diagnoses from the use-case list, changing APGAR to a clinical assessment tool example, and adding a Boundaries and Relationships section.
additional_context: Observation and Condition are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Later Published issues refined the same boundary family: FHIR-8872 clarified symptom/complaint guidance in Condition, FHIR-26904 added further Condition-vs-Observation clarification, and FHIR-39190 aligned Observation boundary text with Condition language. Community searches found no direct FHIR-2964 Confluence reference or contrary decision; later minutes and Zulip discussion describe the same nuanced overlap.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Current Observation source explains measurements and subjective point-in-time assessments, includes clinical assessment tools rather than diagnoses in the use list, and says diagnoses typically belong in Condition while Observations may support Condition assertions. Current Condition source describes conditions, problems, diagnoses, concerns, and tracked health issues, and explains when subjective/objective findings and symptoms are typically Observations versus Conditions.
